summary: Mara introduced herself. Left corporate law 4 months ago to do ceramics full time. Father stopped speaking to her properly after she quit — functional texts only ('OK', 'stay warm'). Business is slow, 2 months in. Mentioned the Cascadia Craft Fellowship grant — a local grant for people doing exactly what she's doing — but hadn't applied yet. Admitted her studio has been obsessively clean, which is how she knows things are bad: when everything is in its place, she's too in her head to make anything.

First real paying client: a restaurant downtown commissioned twelve custom place settings. Father visited the studio for the first time — looked around for ten minutes, said almost nothing, left. Mara described it as 'the most expensive silence I've ever heard.' Submitted the Cascadia grant application. Mentioned wanting to take a hand-building technique class to fix a weakness in her larger-scale pieces.

Got the Cascadia Craft Fellowship grant. Father called — he'd seen one of her pieces at a friend's home and called to say he thought it was beautiful. Mara has been sitting with that for two days. The large platters for the restaurant commission came out better than expected — she thinks she's finally figuring out the scale problem on her own. Session is ongoing.
